As you probably know, if ANY certificate authority is compromised, they're all compromised.

Mmm, no, not any.

It's a branch based hierarchy. Wherever a compromise takes place, it affects the trust relationship for all those below it, not above.

If you have a cert issued by Verisign and Digicert is compromised, I can issue certs for your service through Digicert that your devices will accept the same way they would accept your Verisign cert. You can of course use pinning and whatnot, but those are special use cases for narrow scenarios.

If ANY trusted or intermediate certificate authorities are compromised, you can no longer trust the typical indicators of site security; Little green padlocks, etc.

Worst part about all this is that SSL certs cost an arm and a leg. Especially if you want a e-retailer verified cert. I don't run ads on my site anymore, but that means I'm 100% covering the cost myself.. they're not super popular sites either so it gets hard to sustain.
